notes:
User is planning a large, multicultural dinner party and enjoys experimenting with rice and noodles. The evolving menu includes Korean BBQ beef, Middle Eastern falafel, Indian samosas and saag aloo, plus kimchi and bokkeumbap. They previously discussed scalable Korean dishes (bulgogi, galbi, dak galbi, pork belly), Indian options (chana masala, palak paneer, tandoori chicken, biryani), and Middle Eastern foods (falafel, shawarma, hummus, tabbouleh).

User chose traditional Indian basmati rather than the Japanese short-grain rice they have been using. They enjoy trying different rice varieties and will buy basmati from a store. Useful brands previously mentioned: Tilda, India Gate, Daawat, and possibly Lundberg; advise choosing long, slender, aromatic grains and adjust soaking/cooking instructions.

For falafel, user wants a crisp exterior and fluffy interior. Recommendations: use dried chickpeas soaked overnight rather than canned; pulse coarsely without making paste; chill the mixture; avoid overcrowding; and double-fry. Traditional falafel needs no egg, flour, panko, or other binders—use herbs, spices, and baking soda instead.

User enjoys Korean noodle experiments, especially sweet-potato noodles. Suggested dishes include naengmyeon, bibim naengmyeon, ramyeon, jjajangmyeon, japchae, kalguksu, and haemultang. They have tried four Korean restaurants and reported enjoying excellent bibimbap, a very spicy kimchi stew, and distinctive, tasty japchae with sweet-potato noodles. Continue asking about other dishes they enjoyed or want to recreate.

User recently heard that a new Indian restaurant opened in their neighborhood and wants to try it because the chicken tikka masala is reputed to be excellent. Their city and the restaurant’s name are unknown, so do not invent a recommendation; ask for the name/location or offer to help evaluate reviews and menu if they share it.
